name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.24
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.24**: Bluetooth always sends standard SBC, and the battery shows the right level after charging while switched off.

## Fixed
- **Battery level after charging while switched off** ([#113](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/113)). A player that was charged while off and started later, off the charger, still showed the old lower percentage, which looked like a drained battery. It now shows the level it measures at the start.

## Changed
- **SBC XQ is gone; Bluetooth sends standard SBC** ([Y2Reborn #123](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/123)). XQ and XQ+ sent much more data than headphones and speakers on a busy or weak link could take, and the music stuttered. The **SBC Quality** row in the service menu is removed. A player that was set to XQ uses standard SBC after the update, with nothing to do. **SBC Auto Rate** stays. AAC and LDAC are unchanged.

## Behind the scenes
- **Error reports now show Bluetooth's data rate over time**, so a stutter can be matched to what the link did ([#99](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/99), [Y2Reborn #87](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/87)).

Everything from [Beta 9.3.23](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/releases/tag/baseline-234) is included: Now Playing's progress wave in the cover's colour, the screen that stays dark after a sleep that didn't work, steadier Bluetooth on a weak signal and Wi-Fi on channels 12 and 13.

## Known issues
- A network on channel 12 or 13 may need a second scan to appear.
- Music can stutter for a few seconds while Wi-Fi switches on.
- Far from the headphones the music still pauses when the signal is lost; it no longer rushes afterwards.
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- One audiobook file longer than about 36 hours may not play or not show up; split it into parts of up to 30 hours.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause isn't found yet.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

More details in plain words: **[Beta 9.3.24 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.3.24.md)**.

<!-- github-only -->

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now**. Your music, playlists, settings, Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth pairings stay. (On Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.)

## Install with the Innioasis Updater (easiest)
The community **Innioasis Updater CE** installs Y2Linux for you, on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. No SP Flash Tool needed.

1. Download Innioasis Updater CE for your computer from [innioasis.app](https://innioasis.app/guide.html#download-updater) and open it.
2. Choose **Y2**, then **Reborn (Y2Linux)** and the latest release.
3. Click **Install / Restore**, switch the Y2 off and connect it when the updater asks. Wait until it confirms, then unplug.
4. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** `system.img` from the Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0 into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Step-by-step guides for each computer: [Reborn (Y2Linux) install guide](https://innioasis.app/guides/reborn-y2linux-y2.html). The way back to stock is in the updater too: choose **Y2** and **Original Software**.

## Install with SP Flash Tool
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.24-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

## How it was tested
The platform's full check and Reborn's tests passed, including new tests for a saved XQ setting (read as standard SBC) and for a start after charging while off (63 % saved, nearly full measured). The tests of the release images passed. Not yet tried on a player.

## Files
- `Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.24-first-install.zip`: images, scatter files and checksums for SP Flash Tool. The data image has no SSH key (developers: `tools/production/first_owner.py`).
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `rootfs.ext4.gz`, `bootimg.img.gz`, `recovery.img.gz`: the signed over-the-air update (Ed25519 key `platform-v1-release-20261015`, sequence 16000).

Our own code: Y2Linux and Y2Reborn at tag `baseline-235`. The speaker amplifier driver is Chris Hendrickson's GPL-2.0 AW87559 driver. The headphone profiles are AutoEq results (MIT, Jaakko Pasanen); their licence ships with them.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.21
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.21**: steadier Bluetooth on a weak signal, Wi-Fi on channels 12 and 13, battery and SD card fixes.

## What's new
- **Bluetooth keeps off your Wi-Fi's channel.** Both share one antenna; while Wi-Fi is connected, Bluetooth now leaves the Wi-Fi network's channels alone.
- **FLAC and Opus songs have a bitrate** (skins can show it). For songs already in your library, run Settings → System → Reset & Maintenance → **Rebuild Music Library** once.

## Fixed
- **Bluetooth dropped out and then played fast** when the signal got weak (far from the headphones, a body in between). After a pause in the link the player sent everything it had missed in one burst. The music now simply continues where it stopped.
- **Bluetooth headphones could go silent** after the player was busy for a moment. The player now always sends something while music is on, silence if need be.
- **Starting music on slow Bluetooth headphones** could fail with an error although the headphones were about to answer. The player now waits longer for them.
- **Wi-Fi networks on channel 12 or 13 never showed up.** The player now listens on these channels too; no setting needed.
- **The battery was empty in the morning** on players whose Wi-Fi and Bluetooth never started: such a player could not go to sleep. It sleeps now.
- **An exFAT SD card could freeze until a restart** when a damaged or half-copied file on it was read.

## Known issues
- A network on channel 12 or 13 may need a second scan to appear.
- Far from the headphones the music still pauses when the signal is lost; it no longer rushes afterwards.
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- One audiobook file longer than about 36 hours may not play or not show up; split it into parts of up to 30 hours.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause isn't found yet.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.20
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.20**: audiobooks keep your place, albums play in order, steadier Wi-Fi after waking.

## What's new
- **Previous Chapter / Next Chapter** for audiobooks: hold Select on Now Playing. They jump to the chapter start however far away it is.
- **SBC Auto Rate** in Diagnostics (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times): lets SBC headphones lower the rate when the signal gets weak instead of stuttering. Off by default; if you hear Bluetooth dropouts, please try it and tell us.

## Fixed
- **Audiobooks jumped back to the start of a long chapter** when Previous or Next was pressed by accident (in a pocket, say). The buttons now go to a chapter start only when it is less than 10 minutes away; otherwise they skip 30 seconds. A book you started also keeps its place if you stopped at its very beginning.
- **An album started from the album page played shuffled** when Shuffle was on. A single album now always plays in order; playlists and mixed songs still shuffle.
- **Skins: Cover Flow titles stood still** while the covers slid. They now glide and fade with the covers.
- **Wi-Fi after waking** could give up on a network that was right there and restart, and after a sleep without headphones the player kept looking for them for almost a minute, which held Wi-Fi up. It now looks once and keeps trying a network it can see.
- **A very long audiobook file was missing without a word**: one file of more than about 50 hours is too big for the player to read. Settings → Library now counts it as a file that couldn't be read.

## Known issues
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- One audiobook file longer than about 36 hours may not play or not show up; split it into parts of up to 30 hours (most tools that make M4B files can).
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause isn't found yet.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.16: steady Bluetooth.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
**Bluetooth headphones no longer go silent after a skip, a seek or the end of a song** (#96, Y2Reborn #99, part of Y2Reborn #87). From Play until you pause, the player now keeps a steady stream going to the headphones, as a phone does: music when there is music, silence while the next song gets ready. Before, the stream could run empty for a split second between songs, and AirPods and some other earbuds stayed silent until you paused and played again.

- **Pause:** silence for 3 seconds, then the stream stops. Play within 3 s continues at once.
- **Play** starts the headphones' stream once (it used to start, stop and start it again).
- **One rate for every headset:** 44.1 kHz, and SBC and AAC at one fixed bit rate by default. Codec settings you changed in the maintenance menu stay as you set them.
- **Headphones that drop right after connecting** (for example after pairing them with another device) are no longer reconnected over and over: after three quick drops the player asks you to pair them again.
- Wheel clicks with no music no longer stutter; gapless song changes no longer run the output empty.
- A skip, seek or pause is heard up to about 0.2 s later on Bluetooth than before; that small reserve keeps the stream full.

Before release: all Bluetooth events in 28 error reports read, the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests (new: a simulated pair of headphones that consumes the stream at real time; the old code ran it empty on skips and song ends, the new code never does), a new radio test for headphones that keep dropping, and the 552 tests of the release images. name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.12
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.12: Bluetooth pauses and skips like a phone.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
Beta 9.3.7 kept a Bluetooth stream open while you paused, so that no headphones would be asked to stop and start. Phones never do that, and it caused three complaints at once: silence after a pause or after the second or third song (#89), the connection drop about 20 seconds into a pause (AirPods Pro), and Buds that "disconnected" a minute into a pause (#90, where the player had in fact gone to sleep). This release goes back to what phones and Beta 9.2.16 do.

- **Pause stops the stream, Play starts a new one.** Headphones that went silent after a pause or a skip, and the drop 20 s into a pause, both came from a stream kept open without sound: the headphones run dry and some (AirPods) never recover until a new stream starts.
- **A track change no longer interrupts the stream.** The old song's last fraction of a second plays out and the next follows without a gap; before, the stream stopped for about 60 ms per skip (#89: "the second song is laggy, the third plays without sound").
- **A paused player with Bluetooth headphones stays awake 15 minutes** before it sleeps (#90). The hold was there since Beta 8.18 but counted from the first pause after boot, so a later pause slept after 60 s, and sleep ends the Bluetooth link.
- **No more connect/drop loop for headphones that connect with a different codec than the chosen one** (Y2Reborn #94: Bose SoundLink Flex 2, Sony WF-C710N).

Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests (new ones for the paused-headset hold and the kept Bluetooth sink) and the 552 tests of the release images. On the developer's player with AirPods Pro: skips in a row and pauses of various lengths, all with sound afterwards. A capture of the previous test build showed the packets to the headphones running on without a gap at the skips and silence only after the pause/resume gaps, which is what settled the cause. Other headphones were not re-tested yet: if yours behave worse than in 9.3.7, please send an error report.

body:

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
Bluetooth used to be handled by five separate pieces that coordinated through lock files; when two acted at once, headphones stayed half connected or reconnects stalled. One radio program now owns Bluetooth and the radio it shares with Wi-Fi. The player says what it wants, and the radio program gets there and repairs itself. Every codec, rate and quality setting from 9.2.16 is kept.

- **Codec and quality changes apply without restarting the player** (the headphones are back in about 7–9 s).
- **Your library is no longer emptied when a Bluetooth output fails** (Y2Reborn #92).

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2.14
body:

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
- **Bluetooth no longer drops when you change radio stations quickly** (from an error report): every new station or song closed the Bluetooth output and opened it again, twice, and each time the headphones were asked to start streaming anew. Some earbuds answer that slowly; when one answer took longer than six seconds, the connection ended. The player now keeps the Bluetooth output open from one station or song to the next while the headphones stay the same, as it already did for the headphone jack. Pause still releases it at once.
- **New issue forms on GitHub:** a new issue now opens a short form for its kind of problem (something wrong, slow, battery, sound and Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and radio, install or update, a feature request, a question), so the details needed to find the cause are there from the start.

Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests (new, each failing without its change: a Bluetooth output plays the next stream in the open sink; it is taken only while the headphones' connection, codec, rate and format are unchanged) and the tests of the release images. On the developer's player: installed by update from 9.2.13, and six quick skips on AirPods Pro each played at once in the open Bluetooth output.

What changed and why, in plain words: **[Beta 9.2.14 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.14.md)**. 2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.

body:

Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests (new, each failing without its change: one song from search; a reopened AAC file lands on its place without reading from the start; letter scrolling at a spin; Bluetooth disconnect reasons) and the tests of the release images. body:

- **Menus scroll like lists** (#74): settings pages, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scroll on the screen with a scroll bar instead of inside a box; the Music page scrolls to its last lists.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2.5
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2.5: Wi-Fi finds your network again after a wake.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's fixed
- **Wi-Fi that does not find your network after a wake** (#83): sometimes the Wi-Fi kept searching after the player woke up and never saw your network, and Connect said "not found"; only switching Wi-Fi off and on helped. When Wi-Fi has searched four times over a minute without seeing any saved network, the player now switches it off and on once by itself (at most every ten minutes until it connects). Your Wi-Fi setting stays as you set it.

Tested on the developer's player: installed over the air from Beta 9.2.4 and confirmed by the player itself; Wi-Fi switched off and on the way the player now does it reconnected in 12 s. Before release: the platform's full check (new tests for when Wi-Fi is switched off and on, and when never), Reborn's workspace tests and the tests of the release images.

What changed and why, in plain words: **[Beta 9.2.5 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.5.md)**. body:

## Already running Y2Linux

## What's new
- **Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, charging and computer icons in every skin** (#70, #73). Skins showed only the battery and the clock; all 16 now show the same icons as the standard look, in their own colours.

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2: waking up at once.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Power to wake lights the screen at once.** If you pressed Power to sleep shortly after waking the player, and you have Bluetooth headphones saved that were switched off or out of reach, the next press to wake could leave the screen dark for up to about 20 seconds. The player was waiting for its automatic headphone reconnect to give up before it switched Bluetooth off, and did not look at the Power button while it waited. Now a press to wake is noticed at once, and the player cancels the headphone try instead of waiting for it, so going to sleep takes 1–2 seconds again. Your headphones still reconnect by themselves when they are on.
- **Reset no longer refuses with "plan changed"** when nothing had changed (about one plan in 450: a number in the saved plan was read back very slightly differently).
- In a skin without its own Music page, **Music** opens the Music menu again instead of a plain system page.
- Code clean-ups in the player and the system services that do not change what they do.

Tested on the developer's player: installed over the air from the previous test build and confirmed by the player; all services and Reborn running, health OK, the music player on screen 21 s after the restart. While the player was trying to reach the switched-off headphones, switching Bluetooth off the way sleep does went through after 1.1 s (before: up to about 20 s), and Bluetooth came back on afterwards. The press to wake during that moment is covered by new tests but was not repeated by hand on the player (sleep needs the USB cable out). Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests and the tests of the release images.

## What's new
Beta 9.1 looks and works like Beta 9.0. One small visible change: while an update downloads, the Settings list shows how far it is (*"Downloading · 40%"*) instead of only *"Downloading…"*.

The rest is housekeeping that the Rust rewrite in 9.0 made possible:

The moves were made by script and checked against the original text, so what the code does is unchanged; the same 748 automated tests pass before and after.
- **Small clean-ups in the system services:** shared code where two copies existed, and fewer direct operating-system calls outside the one audited library (82 → 63).

Tested on the developer's player: installed over the air from 9.0 and confirmed; all services and Reborn running, Wi-Fi online, storage and health OK, no warnings in Reborn's log; Reborn's built-in decoder, playback, storage and baseline tests pass on the player; start to music player 37 s (as 9.0). name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.0
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.0: the system underneath, rebuilt.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new

Beta 9.0 looks and works like Beta 8.43. Your music, playlists, play queue, settings, Wi-Fi networks, Bluetooth pairings and Last.fm sign-in all stay. What changed is everything **underneath** the music player. This is the biggest change to Y2Linux since the first beta.

### The part you never see: "the platform"
The Y2 runs two kinds of software. **Reborn** is the music player you see: the menus, Now Playing, the library and the settings screens. Underneath it, **the platform** works all the time: four small background services and one command tool. Between them they:
- watch the battery and switch the player off safely before it runs flat;
- put the player to sleep and wake it, and check afterwards that it really slept and woke on the same start;
- connect and supervise Wi-Fi, keep the clock right, and turn Bluetooth on and off;
- check SD cards before they are used, keep a healthy card read-only between writes so pulling it out can't damage it, and repair or format a card when you ask;
- set up Internal Storage on the first start;
- download, verify and install updates, and undo an update that doesn't start properly;
- show your music to a computer over USB;
- collect and send error reports when you choose to.

Every time Reborn shows the battery, the Wi-Fi state, the storage page or the update page, it asks the platform.

### From Python to Rust
Until 8.43 the platform was written in **Python**, which needs its own interpreter on the player. That had costs you could feel:
- **Every question took about half a second.** Each request started a new Python program, even "is the player asleep?". Reborn asks every few seconds while the screen is on, and so do the Wi-Fi and clock events and every start and shutdown step.
- **CPU time is battery.** While the player was on but idle, the platform alone used about 92 CPU seconds every hour.
- **Memory and space.** The Python services took about 58 MB of RAM, and Python itself 22 MB on the system partition.
- **Two languages talking to each other.** A misspelled field on one side was only noticed when something went wrong. Once this made the player say "wrong password" for a Wi-Fi network that had failed for another reason.

In Beta 9.0 the whole platform is **Rust**, the language Reborn is written in. It's one program of 4.2 MB, with **no Python left on the player**. Every answer the platform gives is now run through Reborn's own reading code before a build is accepted, so a mismatch is caught before it reaches a player (letting the compiler check both sides directly is the next step).

### The numbers
Measured on the developer's player:

| | Beta 8.43 (Python) | Beta 9.0 (Rust) | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU the system services use while the player is on and idle | ≈ 92 s per hour | **≈ 12 s per hour** | about 7× less |
| CPU Reborn uses with the screen off and nothing playing | ≈ 45 s per hour | **≈ 14–16 s per hour** | about 3× less |
| Memory of the system services (counted per process) | 58 MB | **17 MB** | about 3½× less |
| Their real share of RAM (shared parts counted once) | 35 MB | **5.5 MB** | about 6× less |
| Answer to a simple question (sleep, update, battery state) | ≈ 0.5 s | **6–8 ms** | about 70× faster |
| System partition | 130 MB | **111 MB** | 19 MB more free space |
| Update download (system part) | 56.4 MB | **50.6 MB** | 6 MB smaller |
| Press Power → music player ready | ≈ 44 s | **≈ 37 s** | about 7 s faster |
| Shutdown steps after Power Off | ≈ 2.6 s | **≈ 1.2 s** | twice as fast |

What this means for you:
- **Less battery used while the player is on.** It matters most when the player sits on with the screen off: paused, or waiting to go to sleep.
- **Snappier system pages.** The battery, storage, update and Wi-Fi information no longer waits half a second per question.
- **A quicker start and shutdown**, more room on the system partition, and smaller updates.

Battery life *in sleep* is unchanged by this release (see Known issues).

### Reborn got leaner too
- **Quieter when dark.** With the screen off and nothing playing, Reborn now checks things every 5 seconds instead of every second, and reads the battery and storage every 10 seconds instead of every 2. A button press, music starting, a headset connecting or a computer being plugged in still wakes it at once.
- **No more sleep attempts on the charger.** The player can't sleep while a charger or computer is connected, but Reborn used to ask every minute anyway, and each try started a system process. Now it waits until the cable is unplugged; pressing Power still asks at once.

### How we made sure nothing broke
A rewrite like this touches the scariest parts of the system: running out of battery, sleep, and installing updates. So it went in careful steps:
1. **Recorded the old system first.** Every command and every file the platform uses was listed. The old Python platform was then recorded answering **1,069 test situations**: normal ones, odd ones and damaged files. It was also recorded handling **5,729 ways of typing its commands**.
2. **Translated without changing anything.** The Rust version had to give exactly the same answers, byte for byte, before Python was removed.
3. **Fixed what we found**, one fault at a time, each with its own test (list below).
4. **Turned it into proper Rust.** Every file the system keeps is now a clearly defined structure: the sleep record, the update journal, the SD card record, the shutdown request and about fifty more. The computer checks them instead of the code guessing what a field holds.
5. **Checked every step automatically:**
   - about 570 platform tests and 738 Reborn tests;
   - all recorded answers;
   - Reborn reading every platform answer;
   - a check that everything on your data partition stays readable by the previous version.

   That last check is what keeps **Restore Previous System** safe.
6. **22 test builds on a real player**, every one installed over the air and checked on the device.

### Fixes in this release
**Storage and USB**
- **The SD card goes back to read-only right after you unplug a computer.** While a computer was connected, the card's write permission was renewed every few seconds and never closed on unplug, so it stayed writable for up to 30 seconds.
- **A write permission that ran out could leave the card writable** until the next card was inserted or removed. The system now checks for that regularly.
- **SFTP** (file access for advanced users) opened the old music folder instead of Internal Storage.
- **A card with errors** (which plays read-only until repaired) was reported as a failure.

**Updates**
- **Two update checks at once** showed a confusing failure. Now: *"An update check is already running. Try again in a moment."*
- **Restore Previous System on a low battery** was refused but left the update page saying a restore was pending. The battery is now checked first.
- **Radio firmware that could not be installed** now shows as failed instead of looking like success.

**Battery, sleep and Wi-Fi**
- **DNS after an address renewal.** When the router renewed the player's address, Wi-Fi could show *no DNS* for up to five minutes. The DNS servers are now kept.
- **Battery percentage.** In one rare order of battery readings the power service stopped with an error and had to be restarted.

**Damaged files no longer cause internal errors.** A sudden power loss can damage one of the small records the system keeps. Now:
- the status pages stay readable, and the affected item shows as *unavailable*;
- sleep, updates and reset refuse with one clear reason and start a fresh record next time.

A damaged record never decides that something is safe.

### What did not change
- No new screens or settings, and nothing moved in the menus.
- The update installer and the recovery screen, both proven over many updates.
- The kernel (Linux 6.18) and drivers, apart from the version number.

The full story, written for players' owners, with a glossary and a technical appendix: **[Beta 9.0 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.0.md)**. Everything from Beta 8.43 is included.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.0-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md) · Storage: [Storage](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/STORAGE.md) · [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md) · Headphone settings: [Headphone output](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/HEADPHONE-OUTPUT.md) · [Error reports](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/ERROR-REPORTS.md)

## Known issues (beta)
- **A big change underneath:** Beta 9.0 has run through 22 test builds on the developer's player, but not yet on many players. Overnight sleep, a low-battery shutdown, an SD card repair or format and a reset have not been repeated since the last changes. If anything behaves differently from 8.43, send an error report (Settings → Diagnostics); Settings → Diagnostics → **Restore Previous System** goes back to the version you had, with your data kept.
- Battery life in sleep: about 2 mA overnight on the developer's player (estimated from the battery voltage); stock is about 1.3 mA. This release doesn't change it.
- Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on players with empty factory partitions (#62) use the chip's default calibration; please send a report if the range is poor.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause is not found yet. If yours does, start it again and send a report.
- While a large SD card is being checked (up to a few minutes), you can't copy music to it over USB yet.
- The speaker uses the same volume as the headphones; its loudest step is the stock speaker's. Start low the first time.
- Going back to a version older than 8.33 starts with an empty queue (your settings are kept).
- Some car radios don't show the song and artist yet; we are looking into it.
- In a very long single-file book, jumping to another chapter takes 2–3 seconds.
- With very large libraries (100 000+ songs) a list can still take up to about a second the first time right after the player starts, and the first scan of such a card takes several minutes.
- BBC radio stations stream only in HLS, which the player does not play yet (planned for a later beta).
- FM radio is in the works for a later beta.

## Files

## What's new

- **Go back to where the music came from (#60, #25):** Now Playing's menu (hold the center button) has **Go to Playlist**, Go to Folder, Go to Search, Go to Genre or Go to Songs, depending on where you started the music, and opens it with the playing song selected.
- **Leaving Search is easy again (#51):** Cancel always leaves Search, also with text in the box, and holding Back while typing does too. Both go back to where you opened Search.
- **No more duplicate albums (#45, #46):** an album where only some songs have the Album Artist tag is listed once.
- **Albums by artist (#56):** Settings → Customize → **Album Order**: Title or Artist (then title). Cover Flow follows it.
- **Faster scrolling in long lists (#30):** spin the wheel fast in Songs, Artists, Albums or Folders and it jumps letter by letter; the letter stays for a moment after you stop, so you can turn back without losing it.
- **Cover Flow in light skins (#57):** the shelf under the covers now fades into the skin's background instead of black.
- **Headphones unplugged (#62):** the player now says "Headphones unplugged. Playback paused."
- **More haptic feedback (#28):** a tick when a computer connects and while you hold Previous/Next to seek (with Haptics on in Customize).

Everything from Beta 8.42 (sleep, large SD cards, report fixes, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on players with empty factory partitions) is included. Thanks for all the requests!

## What's new
- **Power puts the player to sleep without the screen lighting up again.** The screen goes dark at once, as on the stock firmware. A second press while it gets ready wakes it straight back to where you were, and a sleep the player has to refuse (for example while charging) keeps the screen dark instead of turning it back on.
- **Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on newer players (#62):** some Y2s from 2026 (without FM radio) came with two empty factory partitions, and the radios never started. They now start with the chip's built-in defaults, as on the stock firmware.
- **Large SD cards play at once.** A card with tens of thousands of songs (over about 72 000 on a 1 TB card) was kept read-only and offered for a Repair that changed nothing. The card is now checked in the background while your music plays; only a card that really has errors asks for Repair.
- **Faster restarts with a big library:** after a restart the player no longer reads every unchanged folder again. If you edit tags on a computer, use Settings → **Scan for Music** afterwards.
- **Bluetooth headphones after a sleep:** pressing Play in the seconds before your headphones reconnect no longer plays on the speaker (or the empty jack). The player waits for them and plays there.
- **Wi-Fi:** no more "wrong password" when the password is right, and the player reconnects to your saved network by itself after a sleep or start, without tapping it.
- **Updates (#63):** an update that hung on "Installing Update" now restarts and finishes by itself, and the first start after an update no longer falls back to the rescue screen.
- **Restart and Power Off** can no longer hang with the screen dark (one player drained a full battery that way); if anything stalls, the player completes the restart or turns off by itself.
- **Battery:** the percentage stays right after a restart or update (it could show 13 % instead of 95 %), and the player now sleeps at low battery instead of staying awake and draining faster.
- **Holding Power right after waking** shows the power-off ring instead of cutting the power.
- **The screen at start:** a screen that stayed dark from power-on (seen once on an ST7701S player) is restarted by itself.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.39
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.39: Folders by file name, Shuffle Albums, playlist Sort, big libraries.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Folders like a file manager**: a folder lists its folders first, then its songs, both by name, with numbers in number order ("2 - Intro" before "10 - Outro"). Songs show their **file name**, not the title tag, so loose songs and compilations without an album artist are where you put them. Picking a song plays that folder in the order you see (Next is the row below); Play on a folder plays its folders, then its songs.
- **Shuffle Albums**: Shuffle is now Off, Songs or Albums (Now Playing and Settings → Playback). Albums play whole, each in its own order, the albums in random order. Hold Select on a folder, artist, genre or playlist for Shuffle Albums there too.
- **Sort for playlists**: hold Select on a playlist or one of its songs → Sort: Playlist Order, Album, Artist, Title or File Name. It changes what the page shows and plays, not the file.
- **Big libraries stay quick**: tested on the player with 120 000 songs. Folders open at once, playing or shuffling a whole card takes a fraction of a second, Cover Flow spins smoothly, Playlists no longer search the whole card on every visit, and the long lists are made ready while the screen is off.

Everything from Beta 8.38 (Bluetooth resume, the live wave) is included. Thanks for the report!

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.39-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.35
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.35: louder headphones.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Louder headphones.** The headphone output was capped well below what the player can do, so IEMs and demanding headphones could be too quiet even at High. Each Headphone Level now opens up more of the chip: at full volume **Low ≈0.35 V** (earphones and IEMs), **Medium ≈0.71 V** (as loud as stock, most headphones) and **High 1.73 V** (the chip's maximum, hard-to-drive headphones). Thanks for the report!
- **Safe by default.** Nothing gets louder by itself: after the update your volume number changes so the music stays exactly as loud as before. Turning the volume up past the old maximum asks once (*Raise the Volume?*); after 20 hours of loud listening the player asks again and turns the volume back down. After a restart, or when you switch back from Bluetooth, the volume starts no higher than the old maximum.
- **Changing the Headphone Level keeps the loudness.** A higher level lowers the volume number to match; turn the volume up for more.
- **Even volume steps.** Every click of the wheel is now 1.2 dB, all the way down; quiet listening on IEMs no longer jumps in big steps.

Everything from Beta 8.34 (the MTP fix) is included.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.35-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.33
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.33: a new search and a new play queue.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Search is one page.** The first results show above the keys while you type. Press up from the top row of keys, turn the wheel or press **Search** and the keys fold away: everything found is listed under Artists, Albums, Audiobooks and Songs, with **Play All** for the songs. Select the search field to type again.
- **Your queue plays first.** **Add to Queue** now puts songs right after the ones you queued, before the rest of the album or list (it used to add them at the very end). **Play Next** puts them on top.
- **No more hiccups.** Adding, removing or moving songs, Shuffle and Repeat no longer restart the song that is playing.
- **Up Next is new.** It opens on the song playing; scroll up for the last 50 songs you heard, and below come your queue and the rest of what plays, each under its own heading. Hold Select on a song for Play Next, **Move** (turn the wheel to carry it anywhere, Select to put it down), Remove, Add to Playlist and more.
- **Select Songs.** In Up Next, Songs, an album or a search, hold Select → **Select Songs…**, tick several songs and act on them together: Play Next, Add to Queue or Remove, Add to Playlist.
- **Whole albums, artists, genres and folders** (and a search's songs): hold Select on them for Play, Shuffle, Play Next, Add to Queue and Add to Playlist.
- **Shuffle** now shuffles what is playing right away, and turning it off goes back to the album's order. With Repeat All, Next on the last song starts over; Previous on the first song starts it again instead of stopping.
- Now Playing shows which song comes **next**.
- Songs tagged with several artists ("A;B", "A feat. B") are listed under each of them, and an album shows up once.

Thanks to everyone who asked for these (#60, Y2Reborn #26, #31, #32, #38)!

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.30
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.30: Bluetooth headphone volume, Previous restarts the song, no audiobooks in shuffle.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Bluetooth headphones follow the player's volume** ([Y2Reborn #22](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/22)). Headphones that support it (AVRCP absolute volume, most current ones) now get their own volume set by the wheel instead of the player turning the music down in software, so they can reach their full volume. Changing the volume on the headphones moves the player's volume too. The wired volume is kept separately. When headphones take over, the loudness stays about where it was. Headphones without this feature work as before.
- **Previous starts the song again** ([Y2Reborn #21](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/21)). More than 3 seconds into a song, Previous goes back to its start; press it again to go to the previous song (like Y2Player and the iPod). Headphone buttons and car controls do the same.
- **Seeking is more reliable.** A seek (holding Previous/Next, or the new restart) could be undone by the song that was still playing and continue where it was; it now lands where you asked.

## What's fixed
- **Audiobooks no longer play in music shuffle** ([#58](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/58)). Shuffle and Play from All Songs, a genre, an artist or a folder only queue music; audiobooks stay in Audiobooks.
- **Songs plays in list order** ([Y2Reborn #21](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/21)). A song picked in Songs is now followed by the next song in the list (A to Z), not the next song of its album.
- **No more cut-off messages** ([#55](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/55)). The update screen said "This takes less than a minut"; every line on that screen now fits. name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.26
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.26: fixes from your error reports — no more switching off on the charger after the battery ran down, Wi-Fi on at the first tap.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's fixed
Twelve error reports sent from players were reviewed; thank you for sending them.
- **The player kept switching itself off after the battery ran down, even on the charger.** One player turned off at 5 %, was charged, and then turned off again a few seconds after every start for about 13 hours, because it reused the 5 % it had shown before switching off. On a charger it now shows the battery's real level, and the 5 % switch-off applies only on battery (a charger that can't keep up is still caught by the voltage limit).
- **Wi-Fi turned on after the player had slept with Wi-Fi off showed "Off" again, or "interface disabled", until a second tap.** It now connects at the first tap.
- **Simple chargers and charge-only cables charged at only 70 mA**, less than the player uses while awake, so it ran down while showing "Charging". They now get 450 mA, the same as a computer's USB port.
- **Shutdowns and restarts leave a step-by-step trail** for error reports. Two update restarts in all reports lost their last records and one stopped until the player was switched off by hand; the next one will show where it stops.
- A harmless Wi-Fi warning when the player re-joins the router no longer appears.
- Error reports say more about "saved network not found" and about SD cards that are refused, and song names like "1.0" no longer garble version numbers in reports.

Everything from Beta 8.25 is included.

You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.26-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.25: the headphone DAC's crystal starts like on stock, and gets more chances when it doesn't.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux

## What's fixed
- **No sound from the headphones on some players** ([#52](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/52), [#54](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/54)). On two players the DAC's clock crystal didn't start when Y2Linux powered the DAC, sometimes right after switching on, so songs "played" without sound. Stock powers up the whole DAC chip when it starts the crystal; Y2Linux powered only the clock parts. If the crystal still doesn't come up, the DAC is switched off and on again (up to three times at power-up, plus once more when a song starts), so a slow crystal gets another chance instead of staying silent.

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.24: headphones play everything at 44.1 kHz, like stock.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## What's fixed
- **Headphones going silent after skipping on some players** ([#52](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/52)). For players without Wi-Fi, whose clock otherwise starts at the release date after every restart. The time is kept across restarts; as soon as Wi-Fi brings the network time, that wins.

## What's fixed
- **Headphones silent or "Playback could not start" on some players** ([#52](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/52), [#54](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/54)). The headphone DAC runs from a small crystal. On some players it needs longer to start, or stops when warm and pushed by quick skipping, and Y2Linux gave it about a second at every Play and changed its clock at every track. It now runs like on the stock firmware: the crystal starts when the player starts, keeps running while you use the player (it rests after two idle minutes) and is no longer switched at every track change. If your player had this problem, please update and send an error report after listening for a while.
- **"Downloading Update… Keep Wi-Fi on." forever.** A download that was interrupted (for example by the battery running out) left the update page stuck, also after a restart. It now says "Update Didn't Finish – Nothing was changed on your player" with Check for Updates.
- **Headphones refused to start right after waking** ("busy", then Bluetooth or an error): the player now lets music start as soon as the screen is back, and tries a busy output again for two seconds.
- **Bluetooth playback dead until a restart** after headphones dropped out while switching codec. It now recovers when they reconnect.
- **Pair refused** ("operation in progress") while the player was reconnecting to other headphones; it now waits its turn like Connect.
- **No sleep for the rest of the day after one harmless kernel warning** (a player stayed awake for hours on a weak charger). A Wi-Fi shutdown race that caused such a warning is fixed too.
- **Updates that rolled back on some players** (the new system did not start twice in a row, seen on two GC9503V players): the recovery now turns the screen off before restarting into the new system, like a normal restart. The first boots after an update now also leave a record of how far they got, so if it ever happens again an error report shows where.
- Error reports: Wi-Fi failures keep their reason and the last failure, logs are no longer flooded by display messages (reports covered only the last minutes), quick track skips no longer list every queued song as unreadable.

Everything from Beta 8.21 is included.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.21
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.21: headphones on players with a slow DAC crystal.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's fixed
- **Headphones: "Playback could not start" / "ALSA -110: Connection timed out"** ([#52](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/52), [#54](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/54)). On some players the headphone DAC's crystal takes longer to start than Y2Linux allowed. The stock firmware simply starts the crystal when the DAC powers on and never checks it; Y2Linux only started it when a song opened, gave up after a fraction of a second and restarted it from scratch on every retry, so a slow crystal never got going. The crystal now runs like on stock: it starts when the DAC powers on, keeps running until the DAC powers off, and a song waits up to 1 s for it and then plays anyway. Skipping tracks no longer restarts it. Beta 8.20's stronger crystal drive is gone (it did not help).
- The DAC now stays powered for 5 s after a song stops, so track changes don't restart it.
- Error reports show the crystal's state (ready, unconfirmed starts, errors).

If you had #52 or #54: please update and send a report after playing for a while, whether it works or not.

Everything from Beta 8.20 is included.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.21-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.19: audiobooks, sharper covers and Customize.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux

## What's new
- **Audiobooks.** Put books in a folder named `Audiobooks` (or `Hörbücher`), use `.m4b` files, or tag them with the genre *Audiobook*, and **Home → Audiobooks** appears. Books you are listening to come first, with *Chapter 3 of 12 · 45 %*; a book's page shows its chapters and how long it still runs. Books never show up among your songs, albums or artists, and they are not scrobbled.
  - **Chapters:** the chapter marks inside M4B and MP3 files, otherwise one file per chapter. Next and Previous move by chapter; holding them winds through the book in big steps.
  - **Your place is kept for every book**, also across restarts and updates and after renaming a folder; when you continue, the book goes back a few seconds (more after a long pause). A finished book starts over.
  - **Speed:** 0.75× to 2× per book, without changing the voice's pitch (hold Select on Now Playing → Speed).
  - **Very long single-file books play** (they used to stay silent beyond about 9 hours), and M4B files that carry their cover as a video track are no longer refused.
  - Guide: [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md).
- **Sleep timer**, for music and books: hold Select on Now Playing → Sleep Timer → 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes (it fades out) or the end of the chapter or song.
- **Sharper covers.** Covers are shown at the size they are drawn, scaled with a better filter, and small covers in lists are made from the full picture. Wide or tall covers are cropped to their centre instead of stretched. The cover cache holds 3 000 albums (it is rebuilt once after the update). For your own files: square covers of 300–600 px look best.
- **Settings → Customize** (new):
  - **Wrap Around:** menus continue at the other end (Menus, the default), also long lists (Everywhere), or not at all (Off). A fast spin through a long list stops at its end first.
  - **When Screen Off:** what the wheel and its buttons do in the dark: *Locked* (safe in a pocket), *Buttons* (Play/Pause, Previous/Next; as before), or *Wheel + Buttons* (also the wheel as volume and the centre as Play/Pause). Power, the volume keys and headphone buttons always work.

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.17: fixes from your reports.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Headphones keep working after a pause (#51).** After pausing, locking the screen and pressing Next, the headphones could go silent with "Playback could not start: ALSA -110" until a restart. The headphone chip's clock now keeps running between songs, as on the original firmware, and if it ever fails to start the chip is powered off and on once before giving up.
- **SD cards that a computer reads are no longer refused as "needs repair".** A card that was pulled out or switched off while in use often carries small leftovers (a stale free-space count, a renamed label, a few unused clusters) that Windows ignores; the player now accepts those too and only refuses real damage. A card that is just slow to check says so instead of "needs repair", and songs on a refused card no longer ask you to reinsert it.
- **Bluetooth headphones that drop out no longer block every button.** If the connection was lost at the wrong moment, every button could say "Couldn't complete that" until a restart. The player now notices, pauses and switches back to the headphone jack.
- **Bluetooth search and Connect work on the first press.** Search no longer fails the first few times, and Connect waits for (and cancels) an automatic reconnect to other headphones that are switched off, instead of saying an operation is in progress. Paired devices don't need a new search: pick them and press Connect.
- **Steadier sound on weak Bluetooth speakers.** With SBC (most soundbars and receivers), the player now lowers the bitrate step by step when the link struggles and raises it again when it recovers.
- **Smaller fixes:** a failed update check is retried within the hour instead of the next day; your own radio stations recognise playlists served as plain text, and the reason a station fails is logged; a Bluetooth pause no longer logs a fault; error reports carry more evidence for Wi-Fi not finding your network after a wake, rare dark screens after a wake, and SD card checks.

Thanks to everyone who sent reports, opened #51, or posted on Reddit — every item above comes from them.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.16
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.16: big music libraries.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
- **Big libraries play from All Songs again.** With more than 20 000 songs, every song picked from All Songs said "Couldn't complete that". The play queue now holds up to 5 000 songs: picking a song queues it with the songs around it, and **Shuffle** plays a random 5 000 from the whole library (press Shuffle again for another 5 000).
- **Much faster library scans.** On a 28 600-song card the player spent about 12 minutes after every start checking songs it already knew; that now takes seconds plus the time to look through the folders. New songs are read on several processor cores at once, at low priority, so music keeps playing smoothly.

Thanks to the user who sent the report with the timings that showed where the time went.

Everything from Beta 8.15 is included.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.16-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

body:

## Already running Y2Linux

## What's new
- **Shuffle is really random now.** Every Shuffle used to play the same order, because the order was worked out from the song instead of from chance, and Shuffle on an album or playlist always started with its first song. - **Seeking starts small.** Holding Previous or Next used to jump 30 seconds about ten times a second. It now moves 1 second at a time, speeds up to 3 and then 10 seconds the longer you hold, and never jumps more than about a sixtieth of the song.
- **Shuffle on genres.** A genre now has a **Shuffle** row under **All Songs**, as on an album.
- **Long song titles on the Home screen** now end with "…" instead of running into the menu.
- The automatic Internal Storage setup no longer logs a harmless storage error, which used to send a false error report.

- **Music apps see your songs over USB.** Apps that read a player's song list over MTP, such as Strawberry, found no songs on the Y2, so music on the SD card seemed to be missing. body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.12: crash loop, silent audio and sleep fixes.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

**Stuck in a loop with a garbled screen, or updates that undo themselves ([#49](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/49))?** Take the SD card out, hold Power for 10 s and turn the player on again, install this update, then put the card back.

## What's new
- **No more crash loop from a playlist on the SD card** ([#49](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/49)). A playlist (`.m3u`/`.m3u8`) with a character such as `’`, `º` or `é` at one particular place in a line made Reborn crash a few seconds after every start. The screen was left garbled, and an update couldn't confirm itself, so it was undone. Such playlists now open normally (Windows-1252 files too), and entries that aren't on the player say so.
- **One odd file can no longer stop the player.** A crash while reading a single playlist, cover picture or song now skips that file instead of stopping Reborn.
- **A clear screen if Reborn can't start.** After five failed starts the player shows *Couldn't Start* instead of a garbled screen. Inserting or removing the SD card tries again; on battery it switches off after 10 minutes instead of draining.
- **No more silence after changing the equalizer** ([#48](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/48)). Each equalizer change restarts the headphone DAC. If its clock crystal was slow to start, the song kept "playing" in silence until the next track. The crystal now gets a second, longer try; if it still fails, the player starts the song again instead of playing nothing.
- **Sleep works again after a refused attempt.** If the system refused sleep at the very first step (which could happen right after the player parked an idle processor core), the player then stayed awake for hours on battery. That first step no longer fails, and a refusal like that is retried after two minutes.
- **A dark screen after an update restart** is less likely: a start-up race could leave the display unable to show anything until the previous version was restored.
- **More useful error reports.** A crash loop sends one report instead of many, triggers that fire together share one report, and the reports finally include the kernel's `/proc` and debug files and the DAC registers, which had been left out by mistake.
- A `system.img` copied into **Firmware** after the radio firmware is already installed is now checked and removed.

Everything from Beta 8.11 is included.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.12-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

- **See a report being made.** Send Report Now and Save Report show their progress like a software update (Collect · Clean · Send or Save), and neither asks for a topic any more: every report holds everything.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.6
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.6: smoother, safer headphone sound and less battery with a headphone profile.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What's new
A review of everything in audio playback after Beta 8.5:
- **No sudden loudness.** A fade-in now continues when you skip, seek or change songs while it runs, and turning the volume up during a fade keeps fading. Sound settings that make the music louder (turning a headphone profile off, a bass preset, switching Normalize Volume) now fade in too.
- **Paused music takes your new settings.** Changing the equalizer, a profile, Normalize Volume or Reset Settings while paused now applies when you press Play (before, the old sound continued). Choosing the Headphone Level that is already selected no longer restarts the song.
- **Less battery with a headphone profile.** A profile no longer holds the processor at a higher speed while music plays, and the equalizer itself uses fewer processor cycles. The sound is unchanged.
- **Profiles for hi-res files.** The automatic volume reduction of a profile now also covers 88.2–384 kHz files; six profiles play up to 0.4 dB quieter because of it. The profile list no longer shows a "LICENSE-AutoEq" entry.
- **Headphone level change made safe in every case.** The kernel never changes the headphone output level while the amplifier is running, even when a song starts at that exact moment.

Everything from Beta 8.5 is included.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## Fixed: a dark screen after a restart
- A restart could leave one of the display's bus clocks switched off for the bootloader. The bootloader's logo then got stuck on the way to the screen, and Linux never got a picture: the screen stayed dark until you held Power for 10 s. name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.0
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 8.0: fixes from the 1.0 review.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## Fixed
- **Updates no longer undo themselves when one song is broken.** A single file the player could not read (a truncated download, a mislabelled `.mp3`) made every library scan count as interrupted; the update's health check then restored the previous version about three minutes after installing. Such files are now simply counted (Settings → Library: *N can't be read*) and the update check asks Reborn whether it is healthy.
- **Songs deleted from a computer leave the library again**, even when a broken file sits on the same storage.
- **Large or slow SD cards mount.** A card whose check took more than about seven seconds was never mounted, and the checks piled up in the background. The check now runs on its own, as long as it needs.
- **Settings survive going back a version.** If an update is rolled back, the older Reborn keeps every setting it understands instead of starting from defaults (the refused file is kept).
- **A stuck installer turns off** after ten minutes on battery instead of keeping the screen on until the battery is empty.
- USB copies: a rare fallback in the fast receive path now stops the DMA engine before the processor takes over, so it can never lose part of a packet unnoticed.
- Internal Storage no longer repeats a refused background write at every start.

Installed over the air on a real player and checked there with a deliberately broken song on Internal Storage: the update confirmed itself and the library kept working.

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 7.8: Last.fm fixes.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## Fixed: Last.fm scrobbling
- **Now Playing stays on your profile:** it is sent again when you continue after a pause or play a song again (Beta 7.7 sent it once per song, so it disappeared after a pause).
- **One bad play can no longer stop scrobbling:** if Last.fm refuses a single play as invalid, only that play is left out and the rest are sent.
- **Signing in right after Wi-Fi connects** now waits until the player's clock is set (secure connections need the right date) and says so, instead of failing.
- Pressing Connect twice no longer starts two sign-ins.
- Internet radio, clock (automatic time zone), platform and Last.fm events reach the player's log again, which helps with bug reports.

Last.fm scrobbling itself (new in Beta 7.7) is confirmed working on a real player: QR sign-in and scrobbles appear on last.fm. Guide: [Last.fm scrobbling](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/LASTFM.md).

Everything from Beta 7.7 (Last.fm scrobbling) and earlier is included.

## Already running Y2Linux

## New: Last.fm scrobbling
- **Settings → Last.fm → Connect with Your Phone:** the player shows a QR code; scan it with your phone, allow Y2Reborn, done. The player never sees your password (a password sign-in is there as a fallback; it is used once and not stored).

- **`.scrobbler.log`:** optionally the player also writes the classic Rockbox scrobbler log to Internal Storage, for upload tools — no account needed.

- **Pause and play continue at once:** the player no longer restarts the song after a pause (it used to "buffer" for about a second, on Bluetooth and wired). After three minutes paused it rests the audio as before.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 3
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 3: better Bluetooth sound for AAC headphones, and fewer dropouts on a weak link.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install**.

## What's new
- **Better AAC sound** (AirPods and most other AAC headphones): the encoder's high-quality mode, at the highest rate the headphones accept (AirPods: 256 kbit/s instead of 220). Each audio frame still fits one radio packet, so headphones that can't reassemble split frames keep working.
- **Fewer dropouts:** on a weak link (distance, walls, a busy Wi-Fi) the AAC rate now steps down by itself (256 → 192 → 160 → 128 kbit/s) instead of starving the headphones, and climbs back after about 10 seconds of a clear link. LDAC already did this; AAC now does too.
- **SBC XQ** for SBC-only headphones can be chosen without the experimental switch (System → SBC Quality; the default stays Standard).
- Nothing to set up: the new behaviour is on by default. The System menu has **AAC Quality** and **AAC Auto Rate** for trying the alternatives.
- Faster, cleaner release builds behind the scenes (one build workspace, parallel package builds, sources uploaded only when they change).
