name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 2
body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 2: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi fixes, and the audio output now follows your headphones.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install**.

## What's new
- **Automatic audio output:** Bluetooth headphones take over from the headphone jack as soon as they connect, and music keeps playing on them. When they disconnect, playback pauses and the jack is used again. If you pick the jack by hand, that choice sticks until the headphones reconnect.
- **Bluetooth reconnect:** if your headphones were not around when the player woke up, auto-reconnect used to give up for the rest of the session. It now treats them as simply not there, and they can connect when you take them out.
- **Faster, more reliable radio start:** a race in the Bluetooth/Wi-Fi chip transport sometimes lost a reply from the chip, costing about 4 seconds and a restart of the radio chip. Fixed.
- **Shorter Bluetooth search** for absent headphones (5 s), so Wi-Fi isn't held up after a wake.
- **Wi-Fi passwords** containing `\` or `"` now work.
- Less background work while on Wi-Fi (the internet check runs every 5 minutes instead of every 30 seconds); the player shows up as a music player in Bluetooth lists.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.2-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package onto the **Firmware** drive. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md)

## Known issues (beta)
- Battery life in sleep is not yet stock-like (about 9 mA vs stock 1.3 mA).
- Rarely a slow display start after a restart (the picture starts anyway); if the panel stays dark, hold Power for 10 s.
- The player cannot detect wired headphones yet: "jack" simply means "no Bluetooth headphones connected".
- USB after a wake from deep sleep not yet confirmed over many wakes; AAC with AirPods is negotiated but not yet confirmed by listening.
- The Beta 2 fixes were built and checked on the computer; their device check follows the first over-the-air installs.
- Tested on one hardware revision and one player. A kernel that hangs before its rescue system can only be fixed with SP Flash Tool.

## Files
- `Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.2-first-install.zip`: images, scatter files and checksums for SP Flash Tool. The data image has no SSH key (developers: `tools/production/first_owner.py`).
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `rootfs.ext4.gz`, `bootimg.img.gz`, `recovery.img.gz`: the signed over-the-air update (Ed25519 key `platform-v1-release-20261015`, sequence 5100).
- `…-sources-buildroot-legal-info.tar`, `…-sources-linux-6.18.56.tar.xz`: corresponding sources and licences. Our own code: Y2Linux and Y2Reborn at tag `baseline-51`.
- `SHA256SUMS` for all of the above.

Beta software: use at your own risk. Not affiliated with Innioasis or MediaTek. Details: [Beta 2 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-2.md).

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 1
body:
**The first public beta of Y2Linux and the Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.** Linux 6.18 and a native music player replace the stock Android system; the bootloaders, calibration and factory partitions stay untouched. Ready-made images, one SP Flash Tool pass, then updates over Wi-Fi.

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.1-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package onto the **Firmware** drive. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work and why RECOVERY is flashed once: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md)

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install**.

## Highlights
- Reborn: Cover Flow and album grid, Genres, 15 themes, A–Z sorting that ignores case, accents and "The", click-wheel UI on the GPU.
- Wired playback; Bluetooth with automatic codec choice: SBC, AAC (fdk-aac-free) and LDAC.
- Over-the-air updates: daily check, download with progress and speed, one-minute install with backup, readback and automatic rollback; the player restarts by itself.
- Deep sleep with stock-parity power settings; stock battery percentage and top-off charging; MTP for internal storage and SD card.
- No proprietary MediaTek firmware in any image: each player uses its owner's copy, kept across updates.

## Known issues (beta)
- Battery life in sleep is not yet stock-like (about 8.3 mA vs stock 1.3 mA).
- Rarely a slow display start after a restart (the picture starts anyway since 47); if the panel stays dark, hold Power for 10 s.
- USB after a wake from deep sleep not yet confirmed over many wakes; Bluetooth headphones not always reconnected after a wake; AAC with AirPods not yet confirmed.
- Tested on one hardware revision and one player. A kernel that hangs before its rescue system can only be fixed with SP Flash Tool.

## Files
- `Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.1-first-install.zip`: images, scatter files and checksums for SP Flash Tool. The data image has no SSH key (developers: `tools/production/first_owner.py`).
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `rootfs.ext4.gz`, `bootimg.img.gz`, `recovery.img.gz`: the signed over-the-air update (Ed25519 key `platform-v1-release-20261015`, sequence 5000).
- `…-sources-buildroot-legal-info.tar`, `…-sources-linux-6.18.56.tar.xz`: corresponding sources and licences. Our own code: Y2Linux and Y2Reborn at tag `baseline-50`.
- `SHA256SUMS` for all of the above.

Thanks to @samanz for the headphone-level work and the Reborn improvements in this beta.

Beta software: use at your own risk. Not affiliated with Innioasis or MediaTek. Details: [Beta 1 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-1.md).

name: Y2Linux Baseline 49
body:
Y2Linux Baseline 49 — ready-made images for a first install, and the update for players that already run Y2Linux.

## Already running Y2Linux (46 or later)
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install**. Your Wi-Fi and Bluetooth firmware is kept automatically.

## New install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, this release's **`Y2Linux-49-first-install.zip`** and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis.

1. Unpack the Y2Linux zip and the Innioasis package.
2. SP Flash Tool → Download Only → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download, connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug, press Power: Y2Linux and Reborn start.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer again and copy **`system.img` from the Innioasis package** to the **Firmware** drive. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · why RECOVERY is flashed: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md)

## What's new
- **No proprietary MediaTek firmware in any image.** Each player uses its owner's copy (kept across updates). The system images of releases 46–48 were removed because they contained it.
- One-time flash package with the Y2 recovery image; afterwards everything updates over Wi-Fi.
- Bluetooth codecs: SBC, AAC (fdk-aac-free, AAC-LC) and LDAC.
- Headphone load measurement and two CS43131 driver fixes (thanks @samanz, #38); covers that load reliably, A–Z sorting that ignores case, accents and "The", genre titles on the album grid (thanks @samanz, Y2Reborn #6–#8).

## Files
- `Y2Linux-49-first-install.zip`: images, scatter files and checksums for SP Flash Tool. The data image has no SSH key (developers: `tools/production/first_owner.py`).
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `rootfs.ext4.gz`, `bootimg.img.gz`, `recovery.img.gz`: the signed over-the-air update (Ed25519 key `platform-v1-release-20261015`, sequence 4900).
- `Y2Linux-49-sources-*`: corresponding sources (Buildroot legal-info with package sources, patches and licences; the Linux 6.18.56 archive). Our own code is this repository and Y2Reborn at tag `baseline-49`.
- `SHA256SUMS` for all of the above.

Kernel `6.18.56-y2linux-platform-v1-power-final-49`. Developer preview; use at your own risk. Not affiliated with Innioasis or MediaTek.

name: Y2Linux Baseline 48
body:
Y2Linux Baseline 48 — a new download screen.

Install over Wi-Fi: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install** (charger or at least half a battery).

- Downloads show their step, the percentage, a smooth progress bar, MB downloaded, the speed and the time left, then a short check with its own bar.
- When the download is finished the page turns to **Ready to Install** and a notice says so, wherever you are.
- The download is checked once instead of twice (about 12 seconds faster) and runs at low priority, so music and the screen stay smooth.
- Includes Baseline 47's fix for the dark screen while an update installs.

The new screen appears from the next download on (this download still uses the installed version's screen).

Kernel `6.18.56-y2linux-platform-v1-power-final-48`, release `1.0.0-platform-v1-power-final-candidate.48`, update sequence 4800. Assets: `manifest.json` + `manifest.sig` (Ed25519, key `platform-v1-release-20261015`) and the three payloads pinned by SHA-256. Developer preview.

---
**Note (2026-10-16):** the system image (`rootfs.ext4.gz`) was removed from this release because it contained proprietary MediaTek radio firmware that may not be redistributed. Use Baseline 49 or later; their images contain no firmware.

name: Y2Linux Baseline 47
body:
Y2Linux Baseline 47 — fixes the dark screen while an update installs.

Install over Wi-Fi: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install** (charger or at least half a battery).

- The display's DSI clock gating stays off. With it, the display controller could answer register reads one register late after start-up, so the first picture never started (seen on the installer screen and once at a cold start). No battery cost: the DSI only runs while the screen is on.
- The recovery probe (`y2-platform update probe-recovery`) restarts into the installer screen and back, like an install.

Kernel `6.18.56-y2linux-platform-v1-power-final-47`, release `1.0.0-platform-v1-power-final-candidate.47`, update sequence 4700. Assets: `manifest.json` + `manifest.sig` (Ed25519, key `platform-v1-release-20261015`) and the three payloads pinned by SHA-256. Developer preview.

---
**Note (2026-10-16):** the system image (`rootfs.ext4.gz`) was removed from this release because it contained proprietary MediaTek radio firmware that may not be redistributed. Use Baseline 49 or later; their images contain no firmware.

name: Y2Linux Baseline 46
body:
Y2Linux Baseline 46 — the first release on the over-the-air update channel.

**Players with Y2Linux and the Y2 recovery image** install this from Settings → About & Updates over Wi-Fi: Check for Updates → Download Update → **Restart and Install** (charger or at least half a battery). The player restarts, installs in about a minute, restarts into the new version and confirms it; on any failure it restores the previous one.

New since Baseline 34:
- Over-the-air updates through a Y2 recovery image: signed releases, verified readback, automatic rollback.
- Software restart works (the dark panel after a restart is fixed).
- The display driver detects and recovers a rare dark start.
- Updates make room on their own (old logs, leftover downloads); music and settings are never touched.
- Installing restarts into the installer and back by itself.

First install, or players without the Y2 recovery image: build from source and flash with SP Flash Tool — see [BUILDING](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/BUILDING.md), [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) and [the recovery install](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/architecture/ota-recovery-install.md).

Assets: `manifest.json` + `manifest.sig` (Ed25519, key `platform-v1-release-20261015`) and the three payloads the manifest pins by SHA-256. Kernel `6.18.56-y2linux-platform-v1-power-final-46`, release `1.0.0-platform-v1-power-final-candidate.46`, update sequence 4600. Developer preview.

---
**Note (2026-10-16):** the system image (`rootfs.ext4.gz`) was removed from this release because it contained proprietary MediaTek radio firmware that may not be redistributed. Use Baseline 49 or later; their images contain no firmware.
